Algae ( / ˈ æ l dʒ iː / ⓘ AL -jee , [ 3 ] UK also / ˈ æ l ɡ iː / AL -ghee ; sg. : alga / ˈ æ l ɡ ə / ⓘ ) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. It excludes the land plants ( embryophytes ). Such organisms range from microscopic unicellular microalgae (including cyanobacteria and phytoplankton ) to seaweeds , multicellular macroalgae which may grow up to 50 metres (160 ft) in length. Most algae are aquatic (especially marine), and some form cohesive colonies . Freshwater algae include Charophyta such as the filamentous Spirogyra and the grasslike stoneworts . Most algae are planktons carried passively by water, although some macroalgae have holdfasts for anchorage.
